title: Rav Huna bar Idi
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was Shmuel’s student, as in [Kiddushin 70a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.70a.14), where Rav Yehudah said to Rav Nachman: “Does the Master not hold what Rav Huna bar Idi said in the name of Shmuel?” etc. In [Midrash Tehillim 22:28](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tehillim.22.22) is his precious homily on the verse David said, “Save me from the lion’s mouth; from the horns of the wild oxen You have answered me” ([Psalms 22:22](https://www.sefaria.org/Psalms.22.22)): when David was tending the sheep he found a wild ox sleeping in the wilderness and thought it was a mountain, and climbed on it. When the wild ox woke and stood up, it lifted him to the heavens, and David vowed that if the Lord saved him he would build a Temple a hundred cubits high, like the horns of the wild ox. The Holy One, blessed be He, summoned a lion; when the wild ox saw the lion, it crouched before it; when David saw the lion he was afraid of it. The Holy One, blessed be He, summoned a deer; the lion leapt after it, and then David came down from the wild ox’s horns and went his way. This is what David said: “Save me from the lion’s mouth, just as You answered me from the horns of the wild ox.” But [Yalkut, Tehillim, remez 688](https://www.sefaria.org/Yalkut_Shimoni_on_Nach.688.1), reads Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi.

notes.text: The first link shows Rav Yehudah quoting Rav Huna bar Idi’s statement in Shmuel’s name. Hyman describes him as Shmuel’s student. The English reads במדבר, “in the wilderness,” for the supplied במרבר.

The linked Midrash Tehillim passage is 22:22 and gives the homily to Huna bar Idi. The linked Yalkut at remez 688 has Yaakov bar Iri (אירי), where Hyman reports Yaakov bar Idi (אידי). In both linked versions the wild ox kneels and David descends before his fear of the lion. Hyman gives a different sequence in which a deer distracts the lion. The exact editions behind his readings remain unverified.
